title: Scheduler Shadowplay and Telemetry Convergence Playbook
author: Maya Chen
body:
Summary
This playbook defines the 'Scheduler Shadowplay' experiment pattern and a telemetry convergence protocol for validating scheduler and kernel-scheduling changes against production-like traffic. It combines parallel (shadow) scheduling runs, targeted profiling, and a gated quality checklist so teams can iterate on scheduling policies without risking customer SLAs.

Why this exists
- Scheduler changes (admission, preemption, kernel hints) can introduce subtle latency and fidelity regressions that are hard to detect with unit tests or synthetic microbenchmarks.
- Shadowing real traffic through a non-authoritative (shadow) scheduler lets us compare end-to-end observables while keeping live traffic untouched.
- Telemetry convergence defines statistical checks and gating rules so rollouts proceed only when measurable signals align with safety thresholds.

Scope and assumptions
- Applies to changes in: scheduler policy DSL, kernel selection heuristics, priority mapping, preemption thresholds, and admission controllers.
- Assumes: shadow scheduler can be run in parallel to production pods (no write-side-effects), tracing headers are propagated (trace-id/kvcache-hash), and a profiling instrumentation sidecar is available.

Owners and contacts
- Playbook owner: eng-serving-runtime Scheduling Guild (primary: Maya Chen)
- On-call escalation: runtime-sre team (pager: #runtime-sre)
- Reviewers: listed in metadata above

High-level pattern
1) Prepare shadow environment
   - Deploy a shadow scheduler instance that consumes mirrored decision requests. Shadow scheduler MUST NOT affect traffic (read-only decision path).
   - Ensure shadow pods have the same kernel build (or explicitly labeled if testing kernel changes).
2) Collect baseline
   - Run shadowplay with baseline scheduler to establish reference telemetry for 48h (recommended) or one production peak cycle.
3) Deploy candidate scheduler
   - Switch shadow cluster to candidate scheduler and run for an identical period.
4) Telemetry convergence checks and gating
   - Compute delta metrics (candidate vs baseline) and run statistical tests.
5) Profiling and targeted instrumentation
   - On any significant divergence, run focused profiler sessions using the profiling sidecar.
6) Decision and rollout
   - If all gates pass, proceed to canary with controlled traffic. If not, collect diagnostics and iterate.

Metric and signal catalog
- Latency: p50/p90/p95/p99 for request end-to-end (ms). Primary gating metric: p95.
- Errors: 4xx/5xx within runtime, kernel faults, NVLink reprobes.
- Kernel switch count: average kernel flips per request (should not increase >10%).
- KVCache hit ratio: prefix/KV cache hit % (should not degrade >1.5ppt for high-fidelity cohorts).
- Token throughput: tokens/sec aggregated per shard.
- Resource signals: GPU SM occupancy, memory allocs/sec, swap activity (on-host), CPU steal.
- Cost proxy: normalized per-token GPU utilization estimate.

Gating thresholds (default)
- p95 latency: candidate <= baseline + 10 ms OR no statistically-significant increase (p-value > 0.05 for Mann-Whitney U test)
- Error rate: candidate <= baseline + 0.1% (absolute)
- KVCache hit: no decrease greater than 1.5 percentage points for workloads with >10% cacheable prefixes
- Throughput: candidate >= 95% of baseline under matched load
- Cost delta: normalized per-token cost increase <= 8% (ops must approve >8%)
- Stability: no kernel panics, watchdog resets, or GPU timeout events during the shadow period

Statistical procedures
- Use paired comparisons where possible: align requests by trace-id to compute per-request deltas and run a Wilcoxon signed-rank test for latency deltas.
- For non-paired aggregated signals, use bootstrap confidence intervals (95%) to judge convergence.
- Require at least N=10k matched requests for meaningful p95 comparisons; otherwise extend the shadow window.

Data sources and dashboards
- Primary time-series: runtime.metrics.{latency,end_to_end}_p95, runtime.errors.count, runtime.kvcache.hit_ratio, kernel.switch_rate, gpu.utilization_pct
- Traces: trace.span.runtime_request -> annotate with scheduler.variant and kernel.hints (tag names: scheduler.variant, kernel.tag, shadow.play_id)
- Dedicated dashboards: "Scheduler Shadowplay Convergence" (Grafana) and "Scheduler Shadowplay Diff" (Heatmap). Ensure diff dashboard shows per-cohort comparisons.

Runbook: immediate remediation flow (if candidate fails during shadow)
1) Abort: stop candidate shadow traffic and revert shadow scheduler to baseline.
2) Snapshot: capture a 10-minute high-fidelity profile (pprof + GPU traces) and save a trace sample set with trace-ids.
3) Notify: post summary to #runtime-ops including key deltas and linking the snapshot.
4) Triage: schedule a focused investigation within 4 business hours with scheduling, kernel, and SRE.
5) Rollback plan: candidate must remain off the production decision path until the issue is resolved and a new shadow run passes gates.

Profiling playbook (when divergence detected)
- Step 1: Reproduce in controlled shadow window with load-sculpting tool (load-sculptor-cli).
  Example: load-sculptor-cli replay --corpus=samples/peak-1H --concurrency=120 --trace-ids=./trace-seed.json
- Step 2: Enable sidecar collection: set env SHADOW_PROFILING=enabled and increase trace sampling to 100% for 5 minutes.
- Step 3: Capture: GPU traces (nsys), kernel timeline (ktrace), and runtime CPU flamegraphs.
- Step 4: Annotate: tag traces with reason tags (e.g., preemption-regression, kernel-selection) and add kernel hint dumps.
- Step 5: Analyze: correlate p95 latency spikes with kernel switch counts and NVLink activity. Use causality checklist below.

Causality checklist (common root causes)
- Kernel hint mismatch: candidate suggested a heavier kernel path for mid-length sequences.
- Increased kernel churn: frequent kernel switches per request due to sequence length fragmentation.
- Admission backpressure: new admission thresholds caused head-of-line blocking at dispatcher.
- KV cache coldspots: candidate ordering increases cold-start requests for popular prefixes.
- Resource contention: increased SM occupancy leading to longer kernel enqueue latencies.

Example scheduler policy snippet (YAML)
- name: test-candidate-policy
  admission:
    max_slots_per_shard: 48
    queue_timeout_ms: 120
  preemption:
    enabled: true
    debt_threshold_ms: 5
  kernel_hints:
    prefer_quantized: true
    max_kernel_switches_per_request: 2
  priority_synthesis:
    economic_weight: 0.7
    fidelity_weight: 0.3

CLI example: start a shadow run (ops)
1) Create play:
   rwd ctl shadow create --name=scheduler-shadow-2026-06 --source=mirror-prod --target=shadow-cluster-03 --duration=48h --note="candidate kernel: v2-opt-hint"
2) Switch policy:
   rwd ctl shadow set-policy --play=scheduler-shadow-2026-06 --policy-file=policies/test-candidate-policy.yaml
3) Watch progress:
   rwd ctl shadow status --play=scheduler-shadow-2026-06 --format=wide

Acceptance checklist before promoting candidate to canary
- All gating thresholds satisfied for target cohorts for a minimum of 48 hours (or one peak cycle).
- Telemetry pipelines show <5% missing trace propagation during the shadow window.
- No kernel-level faults or GPU watchdog events recorded.
- Profiling artifacts and a short investigation note uploaded to the shadowplay artifact bucket: s3://redwood-shadowplay/artifacts/{play_id}/
- Approval from runtime-sre and Scheduling Guild leads.

Rollout matrix (recommended)
- Shadow -> Canary 1 (5% traffic, 4h) -> Canary 2 (20% traffic, 12h) -> Gradual ramp to 100% over 72h if no regressions.
- If canary shows divergence, follow rollback immediate remediation flow above.

Operational tips and anti-patterns
- Tip: Align shadow windows to production peak hours for more representative load.
- Tip: Use cohort labels (e.g., small-seq, long-seq, embeddings-heavy) to avoid signal dilution.
- Anti-pattern: Short (15–30 minute) shadow runs; these often miss tail behaviour.
- Anti-pattern: Ignoring KV cache observables; many scheduler changes shift ordering and indirectly alter cache hit rates.

Appendix A — Example diff report fields
- total_matched_requests
- p95_baseline_ms, p95_candidate_ms, p95_delta_ms, p95_pvalue
- errors_baseline, errors_candidate, errors_delta_pct
- kvcache_hit_baseline_pct, kvcache_hit_candidate_pct, kvcache_delta_pp
- gpu_util_baseline, gpu_util_candidate, util_delta_pp
- artifact_link (S3)

Appendix B — Troubleshooting quick hits
- If p95 increases but kernel switch count unchanged: look for NVLink queueing or host CPU starvation.
- If KV hits drop: verify request ordering and any implicit batching changes.
- If errors spike with no latency change: prioritize investigating kernel-level assertions and runtime error wrapping.
